meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: By estimates this costs a lot.
Actually, it is a big problem.

examples.trans: Actually, it is a big problem.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сроченный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('expired').

examples.trans: In the morning I ate expired yogurt.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень просроченный выбор.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть йогурт.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always yogurt.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ъесть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'ate', paired with 'есть'.

examples.trans: I ate all the caviar.
I could eat an elephant!

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'come in', paired with 'зайти'.

examples.trans: Come on inside here, stubborn horse.
Please come in.

examples.trans: Come on inside here, stubborn horse.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('something pleasant').

examples.trans: The sight in here is not very pleasant.

meanings.en: to be patient for a little while, to hold on
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терпеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will endure / be patient', paired with 'терпеть'.

examples.text: Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: We need to be patient a little and work a bit.
Hang on for five more minutes.

examples.text: Послушай меня, Ваня. Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: Listen to me, Vanya. We need to be patient a little and work a bit.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you the boss in here now, or what?
You are a completely irresponsible cook.

examples.text: Михаил Джекович коня в карты выиграл.
examples.trans: Mikhail Jekovich won a horse at cards.

examples.text: А потом мы обо всём поговорим.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'left, went away', paired with 'уезжать'.

examples.text: А потом Никита уехал в Питер.
examples.trans: And then Nikita left for Saint Petersburg.

meanings.en: to take offence, to get upset
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ижаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be offended', paired with 'обидеться'.

examples.trans: Don't take offence, Vanya.
Don't be offended by my words.

examples.text: Да не обижайся ты, Ваня. Сейчас найду подходящую одежду.
examples.trans: Don't take offence, Vanya. I'll find suitable clothes right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не обижайся, для меня это важно.
examples.trans: Do not be offended, this is important to me.

examples.text: Кофе со сливками специально для вас.
examples.trans: Coffee with cream especially for you.
Hot medallions are needed for a guest.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important, mattering').

examples.text: Не обижайся, для меня это важно.
examples.trans: Do not be offended, this is important to me.
It's an important question.
I have important business.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That is it, candidate registration is already closed.

examples.text: А потом мы обо всём поговорим.
examples.trans: And later we will talk about everything.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I understand everything perfectly.
I understand perfectly.
Wonderful! Thank you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'understand', paired with 'понять'.

examples.trans: The Japanese simply do not understand anything.
I understand everything perfectly.
I understand.
